text:
Anya: Heads up — after the RBAC refactor rolled at 09:10 UTC (rbac-migration v2) I’m seeing a customer report where a workspace admin from Org A could list projects in Org B.
Liam: WTF. repro steps?
Anya: Customer supplied this curl: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Org-ID: org-a' https://api.redwood/dev/v1/projects?owner=org-b` and it returned 200 + list.
Morgan: That sounds like implicit role collapse from the new role inheritance change. We changed project:list to inherit from workspace:admin in the migration, right?
Eli: We did. Policy diff was small but the default merge strategy used `union` instead of `strict-override` for role bindings in the namespace resolver. Might have unintentionally broadened scope.
Anya: I’m attaching the stack trace from the proxy logs and the audit id: audit/2026-03-15T09:11:05Z/0a7c.
sec-bot: automated alert — authz-policy-change detected for rbac-migration v2. Reviewed by security: flag=true, severity=high.
Liam: Quick triage: block path — can we flip a feature flag to revert the merge strategy?
DevOps: We have `rbac_merge_mode` in config. Rolling it back for the hosted cluster will take ~8m with canary. Want me to start?
Anya: Yes, please start canary rollback and pause further rollouts.
Eli: I’ll add a short policy patch to explicitly enforce `namespace.strict_inheritance: true` for cross-org reads while rollback proceeds.
Morgan: Meanwhile, run an audit query to find any tokens that exercised cross-org project:list in the window 09:10-09:20. GCP logs index: project-audit.events, query: `protoPayload.methodName:"projects.list" AND timestamp>="2026-03-15T09:10:00Z" AND timestamp<="2026-03-15T09:20:00Z"`.
Liam: I’ll check KMS decrypt logs too — we need to ensure no KMS keys in Org B were used by Org A principals. KMS log path: projects/redwood-prod/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity.
Anya: Customer says no resources were modified, only listed. Still want to treat as sensitive.
Eli: If it’s read-only, brief disclosure notif may be enough but we must know scope. Also check service-account bindings for `svc-project-reader` role; that one was touched by the role refactor.
DevOps: Canary rollback started on host pool us-west-1-canary. ETA 7m.
sec-bot: deploy-bot: rollback triggered by DevOps (run/4621).
Morgan: Good. Also add a transient audit rule: deny `projects.list` unless `requesting_org == resource_org` at the API gateway level — quick WAF rule. I can push a gateway rule in ~15m.
Anya: Agreed. Also, capture the exact tokens and issue a forced token rotation for any tokens that performed cross-org reads. Who owns token rotation?
Liam: I can issue rotations for customer tokens we control. For service accounts, we’ll rotate keys and revoke any long-lived keys that matched the audit query.
Eli: Action items: 1) DevOps — finish rollback and post status (in this thread). 2) Morgan — WAF rule + audit query results. 3) Liam — KMS/logs + token rotation. 4) Anya — customer comms draft. 5) Me (Eli) — prepare policy fix PR and tests.
Anya: I’ll draft a short customer note: apology, we found a policy regression from RBAC refactor, temporary rollback in progress, investigating scope, will follow up with findings and mitigations.
DevOps: Canary rollback complete on us-west-1-canary at 09:18 UTC. Starting gradual rollback to 10% then 50%.
sec-bot: automated-scan: found 12 distinct tokens that called projects.list across org boundaries during window. Listing pushed to internal audit index (link: https://internal.redwood/audit/0a7c).
Morgan: I pulled the list — 9 were human session tokens, 3 were service-account tokens (svc-project-reader). I’ll open an infra ticket to rotate the 3 service account keys immediately.
Liam: KMS check shows no external decrypts of Org B keys; all reads were metadata-level responses. Good news.
Eli: I pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/421 — adds strict_inheritance test and changes merge to `intersection` for cross-namespace perms.
Anya: Thanks. Once rollback complete and service keys rotated, I’ll send the customer note and CC legal/security. Keep me posted here. :thumbsup:
Liam: Noted. After we close, we should add a preflight check in CI to detect union-merge for cross-tenant roles. Prevent future accidental widenings.
Morgan: Agreed. Also add an eval that simulates cross-org queries as part of the migration canary.
sec-bot: incident-severity: elevated -> tracking as SEC-2026-0315-01.
Eli: Will follow up with postmortem template and timeline.
Anya: Thanks team — moving to incident channel for timeline collection but keeping this thread as root.
Morgan: copying logs and audit exports to the incident folder now.
DevOps: rollback to stable completed at 09:27 UTC. All clusters back to pre-migration state.
Liam: I’ll start revoking the 3 service-account keys now and notify affected SREs.
Anya: Great. Closing the immediate exposure window. Will reconvene for postmortem tomorrow.
